THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Heard the learned counsel for both the sides.
2. The only point urged in this appeal is in respect of apportionment of compensation amount awarded by the NC: 2023:KHC:25432 Tribunal among the wife and the parents of the deceased.
The appellant who is the wife of the deceased and the respondent no.4 and 5, who are the parents of the deceased are claiming the compensation.
The Tribunal by impugned judgment has awarded a sum of Rs.25,02,000/- on account of death of deceased-D.H. Narasimhappa.

The Tribunal has also Thippamma vs Chandrashekar on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123706148/
2 awarded equal share to the petitioners and respondent no.4 and 5.

sentences.text: The appellant-claimant has challenged the same in this appeal.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant and respondents submit that Tribunal should have considered the remaining span of the life of the petitioner and respondent no.4 and 5 while apportioning compensation amount.

This being the only ground on which the appeal is preferred, this court holds that the petitioner is entitled for 50% of the compensation amount and the respondent no.4 and 5 who are parents are entitled for 25% each of the compensation amount.

While making this order,
this Court has noticed that petitioner is aged about 36 years and the respondent no.4 and 5 were aged about 55 years and 60 years respectively, at the time of filing of the claim petition before the Tribunal.
Hence, the appeal is disposed off with the above directions.
5. The registry is directed to send back the trial court record to the Tribunal forthwith.

Sd/-
